# m.futures.trades

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Trades of futures contracts, tick by tick.

Call it from a session `m`:

```python
m.futures.trades(symbols, *, venues=frozenset(dm.FuturesVenue))
```

- Query methods: `blink()`, `append_only()`, `ring()`, `last_by()`, `history()`
- Read from: REST, flat files, WebSocket

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows the [shared rules](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Contract tickers such as `"ESZ5"`, a contracts table, or `dm.ALL`. |
| [`venues`](README.md#venues) | The exchanges whose flat files `history()` reads. |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description | Read from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The futures contract identifier, including the base symbol and contract expiration (e.g., GCJ5 for the April 2025 gold contract)."; flat files `ticker`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under."; WebSocket `sym`: "The ticker symbol for the given future." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Date` | String | The futures session the row belongs to (its trading date), as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: Massive's `session_end_date` from REST and the flat files. The WebSocket sends none, so a streamed row gets the session Massive's futures schedules place it in (between two sessions, the next one). A row they cannot place has a null Date, since the 17:00 Chicago rule can be wrong around a holiday, and the stream keeps running: a spread, a contract whose schedule lookup failed or did not load before the stream opened, or a row outside the loaded schedule logs a WARNING (once per product and date); a contract still being looked up (one a live watchlist or dm.ALL adds) logs at DEBUG only; a row with no readable symbol has a null Date too. From REST and flat files `session_end_date`: "Also known as the trading date, the date of the end of the trading session, in YYYY-MM-DD format." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST and flat files `timestamp`: "The time when the trade was generated at the exchange to nanosecond precision."; WebSocket `t`: "The timestamp in Unix MS." | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Price` | double | The trade price is quoted per unit of the underlying asset, with the total contract value determined by multiplying by the contract’s specific multiplier. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Size` | double | The total number of contracts exchanged between buyers and sellers on a given trade. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `Correction` | long | The trade correction indicator. | flat files |
| `Exchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/futures/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. | flat files |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The unique sequence number assigned to this trade. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
| `ReportSequence` | long | The reporting sequence number. | REST, flat files |
| `Channel` | long | The CME multicast channel this event was sourced from. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST, flat files, WebSocket |
